The stdlib `wait`, `as_completed`, and `asyncio.wrap_future` helpers accept it. `map()` supports `ProcessPoolExecutor`-style chunking. `create()` spawns an owned pool. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pool]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [pymizu.Pool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The pool to wrap. Its lifetime stays with its owner unless `stop_pool` is set, in which case `shutdown()` stops it. [stop_pool]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : When True, `shutdown()` stops the wrapped pool. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} `submit()` and the stdlib `map()` are thread-safe. An internal lock serializes the single-producer pool handle. Use this adapter when several threads submit to one pool. Task failures raise `pymizu.TaskError`. `Future.running()` always returns False because futures resolve at completion. Cancellation follows [`Task.cancel()`](`pymizu.Task`) and never interrupts a running task. `shutdown(cancel_futures=True)` cancels every outstanding future because the pool cannot distinguish queued from running tasks. A running task completes, but its result is discarded. An internal error, such as another caller stopping the wrapped pool, fails every outstanding future. Later submissions raise instead of queueing work. Futures resolve, and `add_done_callback` callbacks run, on pymizu's listener thread. Keep callbacks short. Never block a callback on the pool itself. If the result table is full, `submit()` waits for the executor to collect a result. A submission from a listener-thread done callback raises `SlotsExhaustedError` because waiting there would deadlock the drain. `map()` honors `chunksize` and `buffersize` like `ProcessPoolExecutor`. For bulk maps, [`Pool.map`](`pymizu.Pool.map`) is faster. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Use as a `concurrent.futures.Executor`: ::: {#89185060 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pymizu with pymizu.PoolExecutor.create(2) as ex: futures = [ex.submit(pow, 2, i) for i in range(4)] results = [f.result() for f in futures] results ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 4, 8] ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [create()](#create){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Spawn an owned pool and wrap it. | | [map()](#map){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Return an iterator applying `fn` to every zipped input element. | | [shutdown()](#shutdown){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Shut down the executor. | | [submit()](#submit){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Schedule `fn(*args, **kwargs)` on the pool. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [create()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Spawn an owned pool and wrap it. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/shikokuchuo/pymizu/blob/main/python/pymizu/_executor.py#L165-L187){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature create( n_workers=1, **pool_kwargs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Calls [`Pool.create()`](`pymizu.Pool.create`) with `n_workers` and `pool_kwargs`; `shutdown()` stops the pool. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_workers]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of worker processes for the pool.
